A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison despite pagination changes.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original fine-tuning experiments on SST-2 and CIFAR-100, including rank, accuracy, curvature estimates, and initialization effects.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain the original SST-2 and CIFAR-100 experiments, with numerical tables and training curves.

M1.justification: The LoRA factorization, initialization, regularized objectives, and optimization procedures are unchanged. Newly discussing applicability to LoRA variants does not introduce an algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions use SST-2 sentiment classification and CIFAR-100 image classification. The initialization scenarios and dataset coverage in Appendix C are retained.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparisons retain the same initialization conditions in Figures 2 and 5 and Table 4. Newly cited LoRA variants are not added as experimental comparators.

E3.justification: Reported settings remain identical, including Table 3's optimizers, learning rates, batch sizes and training budgets, Table 4's initialization distributions, and the RSC/RSM evaluation ranks and distance bound.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the weight-decay sweep, rank-dependent RSC/RSM analysis, and initialization sensitivity experiments. Appendix C's rank trajectories and contrasting generalization effects on SST-2 and CIFAR-100 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain the same 1,000-sample Monte Carlo estimation of RSC/RSM constants. Neither adds training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figures 2–5 retain the same results, including SST-2 maximum rank 3 at lambda = 0.01 and RSC alpha = -0.0445 at rank 64. No result entries or empirical findings are added or removed.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 changes the written RSC definition from the self-subtraction ∇_l f(X) − ∇_l f(X) to ∇_l f(X*) − ∇_l f(X). This is a local formal revision, although its sign still conflicts with Appendix A.3, equation (7). No new theorem or substantive proof development is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and central convergence dichotomy remain unchanged. The conclusion newly claims applicability to LoRA+, rsLoRA, PiSSA, and MiLoRA, modestly broadening the stated scope.

C2.justification: The conclusion adds a structural rationale for applicability to LoRA variants and explicitly discusses diagnosing and monitoring fine-tuning. Existing interpretations and qualifications concerning implicit bias, low rank, and experimental applicability remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains the same hyperparameters, proximal-gradient update, singular-value threshold of 10^-4, Hessian-computation restriction, and initialization details. No implementation or code/data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 adds LoRA+, rsLoRA, PiSSA, MiLoRA, and Zhang et al. (2025), while DoRA and LoRA-Pro disappear. The RoBERTa citation changes from Liu et al. (2019) to Zhuang et al. (2021). These are limited updates within the retained research positioning.

P1.justification: There are localized prose and citation-style edits, an expanded conclusion, and new acknowledgments. Theorems replace ambiguous 'full rank' wording with explicit rank r. The section and appendix organization remains substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: All five figures and four tables are retained with unchanged scientific displays. Figure 3 moves before its accompanying results paragraph, and text and float placement reflow across pages; there is no substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Explicitly stating rank r instead of 'full rank' makes the theorem conclusions clearer, and the updated related-work discussion improves contextualization. These are limited gains: experimental evidence and proof substance remain essentially unchanged, and the edited RSC definition still conflicts in sign with Appendix A.3, equation (7), so it does not establish improved theoretical validity.
